title: PACE Center Space and Physical Requirements
canonicalText:
[[PA.1003 | PACE Center Space and Physical Requirements | Applies to: PACE | Revised 02/01/2025]]
<<page 1>>
I. PURPOSE
This policy outlines how the day activity areas for each CalOptima Health Program of All-Inclusive
Care for the Elderly (PACE) Center shall be constructed and maintained to adhere to applicable local,
state, and federal regulations and requirements.
II. POLICY
A. The CalOptima Health PACE Center site shall be constructed and maintained to follow PACE and
  Adult Day Health Center (ADHC) regulations, as well as applicable local, state, and federal
  building requirements to ensure Participant safety.
III. PROCEDURE
A. The CalOptima Health PACE Center shall be designed, equipped, and maintained to provide for a
  safe and healthy environment. Each CalOptima Health PACE Center shall meet the following
  requirements:
  1. Adhere with state and local building requirements;
  2. Be maintained in accordance with the regulations adopted by the State Fire Marshal for the
    prevention of fire and for the protection of life and property against fire and panic; and
  3. Maintain a working, listed telephone service on the premises unless otherwise approved by the
    Department of Health Care Services (DHCS).
B. Alterations to existing buildings licensed as adult day health centers or new construction shall be in
  conformance with all applicable state and local building codes and regulations.
C. The CalOptima Health PACE Center shall comply with general building requirements and state
  regulations as follows:
  1. The CalOptima Health PACE Center’s main activity day area shall be on the first (1st) floor.
  2. Heating and cooling equipment shall be maintained in normal operating condition to provide a
    comfortable temperature.
<<page 2>>
  3. Adequate natural or artificial lighting shall be provided to ensure the comfort and safety of each
    Participant.
  4. Water supply and plumbing shall meet the following requirements:
    a. Drinking water from a private source shall be approved by the local health department at
      least annually. A copy of the most recent health department laboratory report shall be
      available for inspection by DHCS;
    b. Plumbing and drainage facilities, and required backflow preventers (vacuum breakers),
      shall be maintained in operating condition;
    c. Hot water temperature controls shall be maintained to automatically regulate the
      temperature of hot water delivered to plumbing fixtures used by Participants to attain a hot
      water temperature that is not less than 40.5ºC/105ºF and not more than 48.8ºC/120ºF; and
    d. Taps, not accessible to Participants, which deliver water at a temperature of 51.6ºC/125ºF or
      above shall be prominently identified by warning signs in letters at least five (5) centimeters
      two (2) inches high.
  5. Auxiliary lighting facilities, where appropriate, shall be readily available. Flashlights shall be in
    readiness for use at all times. Open-flame types of light shall not be used.
D. The CalOptima Health PACE Center shall be large enough to accommodate all social and health-
  related activities, in accordance with PACE regulations. Space shall be available as follows:
  1. To accommodate both indoor and outdoor activities and for storage of equipment and supplies;
  2. A multipurpose room large enough for all Participants to gather for large group activities and
    meals;
  3. A secluded area set aside for Participants who require bed rest during the day. The secluded
    area shall have at least the following:
    a. Chaise lounges or beds in the number necessary to meet the needs of the Participants and
      upon the written order of the employee or attending provider; and
    b. Rubber or plastic sheeting;
  4. Double-deck beds shall not be permitted;
  5. Space around sleeping accommodations to permit easy passage;
  6. A separate space provided for isolation of a Participant whose illness requires temporary
    separation from others;
  7. Appropriate office or other space provided for administrative and admission activities, for a
    reception area and for a telephone, desk, and file cabinets;
  8. General and specialized storage space maintained to meet the needs of Participants and for
    efficient operation of the center. Storage shall not be permitted in air distribution chambers or
    heating, air conditioning, or ventilating systems; and
<<page 3>>
  9. Space for outdoor activities shall be easily accessible to ambulatory and non-ambulatory
    Participants and shall be protected from traffic.
E. Monitoring
  1. The CalOptima Health PACE Center Manager or designee shall complete quarterly compliance
    inspections and the Program Director shall conduct annual compliance inspections to ensure
    space and physical requirements are met and in compliance.
V. REFERENCE(S)
A. CalOptima Health PACE Program Agreement
B. Title 22, California Code of Regulations (CCR), §§78501, 78503, and 78505
C. Title 42, Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), § 460.72
<<page 4>>
IX. GLOSSARY
Department of Health Care Services (DHCS): The single State Department responsible for administration of the federal Medicaid (referred to as Medi-Cal in California) Program.
PACE Center: The location designated by CalOptima Health PACE at which Participants shall receive PCP services.
Participant: An individual enrolled in the CalOptima Health PACE program.
